title: Coach Josh Boxing
description: Built the full web presence for a boxing gym in Hamden, CT. GymDesk scheduling, automated signups, and local SEO that actually ranks. Next.js from scratch.
longDescription:
Coach Josh needed a site that could convert walk-ins from Google. So I built one.

The gym runs kids classes (ages 6-12), teens & adults, a women's program, and private sessions at $100/hr. I wired up GymDesk for the class schedule and free trial flow so new members can book without friction. Memberships run $100-$175/mo with Stripe handling payments.

The SEO work was the biggest win. I went deep on local search and GEO, and the site now pulls consistently for boxing queries in the New Haven area. That pipeline helped grow the gym past 200 athletes trained. Josh has 37 five-star Google reviews at this point, and the social proof on-site does the heavy lifting for conversions.

I also set up automated outreach. SMS reminders, email sequences for trial signups, and a merch setup for when he's ready to launch that side.

title: Coach Josh Official
description: The digital side of the Coach Josh brand. Courses, an interactive eBook, Mux video, Stripe payments, and a 400+ member community. An entire creator business platform.
longDescription:
This is the product suite I built around Coach Josh's content brand (150M+ views across socials).

The site houses everything:

• Striking Blueprint ($49). Digital guide I designed with an Apple HIG-inspired interactive reading experience. Covers footwork, heavy bag work, head movement, a 4x/week strength program, and printable logs.
• Boxing Blueprint Video Course ($197). 4 modules on striking mechanics, conditioning, defense, and footwork. Mux handles the streaming. Includes everything from the Striking Blueprint.
• Elite 1:1 Coaching ($497/mo). 2-4 private calls per month with custom programming.
• 1:1 Sessions ($100/session). 45-minute single sessions for people who want a taste before committing.
• Discord Community (free). 400+ members, weekly live Q&A, form check feedback.

The tech stack is Next.js + TypeScript with Mux for video, Stripe for subscriptions and one-time purchases, and a PWA wrapper so members can install it on their phones. I also built promo videos with Remotion for launch campaigns.

title: BoxingWiki
description: Free interactive boxing technique library with a clickable muscle map, 60+ techniques, workout generators, and training programs. Think MuscleWiki but for boxing.
longDescription:
I built this because nothing like it existed for boxing. MuscleWiki is great for weightlifting. Click a muscle, see exercises. I wanted that same experience but for fight training.

BoxingWiki has a clickable muscle/body map where you tap a body part and see every technique that uses it. There are 60+ techniques across punches, defense, footwork, and conditioning, each with step-by-step breakdowns, common mistakes, and pro tips.

Beyond the library, I added:
• Heavy bag workout generator with round timers
• Structured training programs with local-storage progress tracking
• Southpaw stance toggle (most resources ignore lefties)
• Flashcard mode for drilling technique names and cues
• Daily streak system to keep people coming back

Built with React + TypeScript and Vite. SEO-heavy with rich JSON-LD schema so individual techniques rank in search. The whole thing is free. No paywalls, no accounts required. Ad-supported with placements that don't interrupt the learning.

title: Enterprise Video Solutions
description: Custom video engineering for NBC, NPR, Forbes, Hedgeye, and others at JW Player. $4M+ book of business. VAST/VPAID ad integrations, DRM, cross-platform player work.
longDescription:
My day job at JW Player. I was the engineer clients called when their video implementation needed to actually work.

I built custom player solutions for some big names. NBC, NPR, Forbes, TMZ, Hedgeye, Guitar Center, Weather Channel, and more. Most of the work involved ad integrations (VAST/VPAID with Google IMA and FreeWheel), DRM/CDM secure playback for premium content, and custom JavaScript player behaviors across web, mobile, and CTV.

Managed a $4M+ book of business. The work was a mix of deep technical problem-solving and client relationship management. Figuring out why ads weren't firing on a specific Samsung TV model at 2am, then presenting the solution to their VP of Engineering the next morning.

I also built out an internal knowledge base across our Frontend and Backend teams, and ran mentoring programs that helped level up the support org's technical depth. Got promoted from L2 to Senior Support Engineer based on the impact.

title: Players Club Community
description: 400+ member Discord community for the Coach Josh brand. Weekly live Q&A, form checks, fight IQ discussions, and accountability. The free tier that feeds the paid products.
longDescription:
The Players Club is the community layer of the Coach Josh brand. It's a free Discord server, but it's the engine that drives everything else.

I set up and run all of it. Channel architecture, bot integrations, engagement strategy, content calendar. The server has channels for form check videos (members post clips and get feedback from Coach Josh and the community), weekly live Q&A sessions, fight IQ discussions, and training accountability.

The strategy is simple: give away real value for free, build trust, and let the community naturally find the paid products (Striking Blueprint, Boxing Blueprint, Elite Coaching). It works because the community actually helps people get better at boxing. The upsell is just offering more depth to people who want it.

400+ members and growing. The engagement rate is solid because we keep it tight. Just people who are serious about getting better.

title: Project Negus
description: A cultural project exploring the African diaspora through art, panel discussions, screenings, and community events. Celebration of our people, by our people.
longDescription:
This was a passion project from my time at Yale. The Negus Project was about exploring the cultures and people of the African diaspora through whatever medium fit the moment. Panel discussions, film screenings, collaborative art shows, community gatherings.

The core idea was simple: celebration of our people, by our people. The unification of us.

We hosted events like a panel discussion breaking down Childish Gambino's 'Awaken My Love!', community film screenings, and collaborative art showcases that brought together students and local artists. I handled art direction, event production, and community organizing.

It ran from 2016-2017 and shaped a lot of how I think about building community. The same instincts I use now when building digital products and working with creators.
